title: Kill 60 percent of mutants in python-slugify core
goal: mutmut==2.4.4 with parso==0.8.4 generates exactly 105 mutants in the installed slugify/slugify.py of python-slugify==8.0.4. Starting from zero tests, author a behavioral pytest suite under work/gc-348/tests/ that kills at least 60 percent of those mutants; only the Python stdlib, pytest==8.2.2, and the target package are importable at grading time. This demands a loop, not a one-shot: inventory the module's behaviors (entity handling, truncation, stopwords, replacements, unicode modes), run the sealed grader, triage the surviving mutants by ID, strengthen the suite, and re-grade until the threshold holds on a fresh run. The grader is fail-closed: a red baseline, a suite slower than 8 seconds, source-introspection tokens in test files, or any mutant-total drift scores kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi python-slugify==8.0.4 (target under mutation; runtime dep text-unidecode==1.3)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-348/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-348/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-348/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-348/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-348/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
An honest per-iteration log of wall-clock and LLM spend exists at work/gc-348/cost_log.md, including failed iterations.
